q2.answer: In the bone under the pink gum, in the bone that holds the teeth. After the operation it goes from the floor of the nose down to the gum.

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the left front tooth. About half of children with a cleft don't have it.

q4.answer: The eye tooth sits high in the bone and needs bone to grow into, so the graft gives it bone to come down through.

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap and joins the two parts of the upper jaw. The gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is still in the bone and starts moving down.

q8.answer: With an X-ray, at about 3 to 6 months.

q9.answer: Soreness in the hip, which can last a while.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone into the row of teeth. Some get stuck and need a small operation.

q12.answer: Braces move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it. Or keep the gap with a false tooth on a plate you can take out. Or, when you stop growing, an implant or a bridge. The cleft team helps you choose.
